arxiv-2106-06630.title: Corruption-Robust Offline Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2106-06630.creator: Xuezhou Zhang, Yiding Chen, Jerry Zhu, Wen Sun
arxiv-2106-06630.description: Abstract We study the adversarial robustness in offline reinforcement learning. Given a batch dataset consisting of tuples ( s , a , r , s ′ ) (s,a,r,s^{\prime}) , an adversary is allowed to arbitrarily modify ε \varepsilon fraction of the tuples. From the corrupted dataset the learner aims to robustly identify a near-optimal policy.

arxiv-2209-02227.title: On 𝒒 \boldsymbol{q} -Middle Convolution and 𝒒 \boldsymbol{q} -Hypergeometric Equations
arxiv-2209-02227.creator: Yumi ARAI and Kouichi TAKEMURA
arxiv-2209-02227.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yumi ARAI and Kouichi TAKEMURA. The q q -middle convolution was introduced by Sakai and Yamaguchi. In this paper, we reformulate q q -integral transformations associated with the q q -middle convolution. In particular, we discuss convergence of the q q -integral transformations. As an application, we obtain q q -integral representations of solutions to the variants of the q q -hypergeometric equation by applying the q q -middle convolution.

arxiv-2403-11371.title: V2X-DGW: Domain Generalization for Multi-agent Perception under Adverse Weather Conditions
arxiv-2403-11371.creator: Baolu Li, Jinlong Li, Xinyu Liu, Runsheng Xu, Zhengzhong Tu, Jiacheng Guo, Qin Zou, Xiaopeng Li, Hongkai Yu
arxiv-2403-11371.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Baolu Li, Jinlong Li, Xinyu Liu, Runsheng Xu, Zhengzhong Tu, Jiacheng Guo, Qin Zou, Xiaopeng Li, Hongkai Yu. Current LiDAR-based Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) multi-agent perception systems have shown the significant success on 3D object detection. While these models perform well in the trained clean weather, they struggle in unseen adverse weather conditions with the domain gap. In this paper, we propose a Domain Generalization based approach, named V2X-DGW , for LiDAR-based 3D object detection on multi-agent perception system under adverse weather conditions.

arxiv-2406-07351.title: Correcting Delocalization Error in Materials with Localized Orbitals and Linear-Response Screening
arxiv-2406-07351.creator: Jacob Z. Williams, Weitao Yang
arxiv-2406-07351.description: Abstract Delocalization error prevents density functional theory (DFT) from reaching its full potential, causing problems like systematically underestimated band gaps and misaligned energy levels at interfaces. We introduce lrLOSC to correct delocalization error in materials over a wide range of band gaps. We predict eleven materials’ fundamental gaps to within 0.

arxiv-2407-11911.title: Energy dependence of the knee in the cosmic-ray spectrum across the Milky Way
arxiv-2407-11911.creator: C. Prevotat 1 , M. Kachelrieß 2 , S. Koldobskiy 3 , A. Neronov 1,4 and D. Semikoz 1
arxiv-2407-11911.description: Abstract The all-particle spectrum of cosmic rays measured at Earth has a knee-like feature around 4 PeV. A priori, it is not clear if this is a local feature specific to the Solar neighbourhood in the Milky Way, or if it is a generic property of the Galactic cosmic-ray spectrum.

arxiv-2409-03284.title: iText2KG: Incremental Knowledge Graphs Construction Using Large Language Models
arxiv-2409-03284.creator: Yassir LAIRGI, Ludovic MONCLA, Rémy CAZABET, Khalid BENABDESLEM, Pierre CLÉAU
arxiv-2409-03284.description: Abstract Most available data is unstructured, making it challenging to access valuable information. Automatically building Knowledge Graphs (KGs) is crucial for structuring data and making it accessible, allowing users to search for information effectively. KGs also facilitate insights, inference, and reasoning.

arxiv-2502-02771.title: When are Diffusion Priors Helpful in Sparse Reconstruction? A Study with Sparse-view CT
arxiv-2502-02771.creator: Matt Y. Cheung, Sophia Zorek, Tucker J. Netherton, Laurence E. Court, Sadeer Al-Kindi, Ashok Veeraraghavan, Guha Balakrishnan
arxiv-2502-02771.description: Abstract Diffusion models demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on image generation, and are gaining traction for sparse medical image reconstruction tasks. However, compared to classical reconstruction algorithms relying on simple analytical priors, diffusion models have the dangerous property of producing realistic looking results even when incorrect , particularly with few observations.

arxiv-2503-16498.title: Llms, Virtual Users, and Bias: Predicting Any Survey Question Without Human Data
arxiv-2503-16498.creator: Enzo Sinacola 1,2, Arnault Pachot 2, Thierry Petit 2,3
arxiv-2503-16498.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a promising alternative to traditional survey methods, potentially enhancing efficiency and reducing costs. In this study, we use LLMs to create virtual populations that answer survey questions, enabling us to predict outcomes comparable to human responses. We evaluate several LLMs—including GPT-4o, GPT-3.5, Claude 3.

arxiv-2505-24484.title: On the Transfer of Completeness and Projection Properties in Truncated Vector Lattices
arxiv-2505-24484.creator: Hamza Hafsi
arxiv-2505-24484.description: Abstract . In this work we investigate the transfer of fundamental order and completeness properties between truncated Riesz spaces and their unitizations. Specifically, we provide characterizations and equivalences for several notions of completeness: the Archimedean property, relatively uniform completeness, Dedekind completeness, lateral completeness, universal completeness, and the projection property.

arxiv-2510-22949.title: End-to-End Design & Validation of a Low-Cost Stewart Platform with Nonlinear Estimation & Control
arxiv-2510-22949.creator: Benedictus C. G. Cinun, Tua A. Tamba, Immanuel R. Santjoko, Xiaofeng Wang, Michael A. Gunarso, Bin Hu
arxiv-2510-22949.description: Abstract This paper presents the complete design, control, and experimental validation of a low-cost Stewart platform prototype developed as an affordable yet capable robotic testbed for research and education. The platform combines off-the-shelf components with 3D-printed and custom-fabricated parts to deliver full six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) motions using six linear actuators connecting a moving platform to a fixed base.

europmc-pmc10329209.title: Physician and Nurse Well-Being and Preferred Interventions to Address Burnout in Hospital Practice: Factors Associated With Turnover, Outcomes, and Patient Safety.
europmc-pmc10329209.creator: Aiken LH, Lasater KB, Sloane DM, Pogue CA, Fitzpatrick Rosenbaum KE, Muir KJ, McHugh MD, US Clinician Wellbeing Study Consortium.
europmc-pmc10329209.description: Importance Disruptions in the hospital clinical workforce threaten quality and safety of care and retention of health professionals. It is important to understand which interventions would be well received by clinicians to address the factors associated with turnover. Objectives

gao-gaoreports-gao-07-919.creator: U.S. Government Accountability Office
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-919.description: Trade Adjustment Assistance: Industry Certification Would Likely Make More Workers Eligible, but Design and Implementation Challenges Exist (2007).

pmc-11309258.title: Successful nonoperative management of a simultaneous high-grade splenic injury and devascularized kidney in Australia: a case report
pmc-11309258.creator: Peter Thanh Tam Nguyen, Jeremy M Hsu
pmc-11309258.description: Severe blunt injuries to isolated solid abdominal viscera have been previously managed nonoperatively; however, management algorithms for simultaneous visceral injuries are less well defined. We report a polytrauma case of a 33-year-old man involved in a motorbike collision who presented with left-sided chest and abdominal pain.

pmc-11539651.title: Efficacy of laparoscopic radical resection of right-sided colon cancer by different surgical approaches: network-meta-analysis
pmc-11539651.creator: Mingyi Li, Jie Hu, Liwei Suo, Hui Wu, Ziming Li, Xiaoyi Xu, Shifeng Zhang
pmc-11539651.description: IntroductionThere are a growing number of surgical approaches for laparoscopic radical resection of right-sided colon cancer, while there are relatively few comparative analyses of the different surgical approaches.ObjectiveTo evaluate the safety and efficacy of different surgical approaches (intermediate approach, caudolateral approach, caudolateral combined with intermediate approach) for laparoscopic radical resection of right-sided colon cancer by conducting a network meta-analysis (NMA).

pmc-11728884.title: Computational exploration of palmitoyl-protein thioesterase 1 inhibition by Juniperus phoenicea L. for anti-dementia treatment
pmc-11728884.creator: Riyan A. Putera Irsal, Gusnia Meilin Gholam, Maheswari Alfira Dwicesaria, Tiyara F. Mansyah, Fernanda Chairunisa
pmc-11728884.description: ObjectivesDementia, a growing concern globally, affects more than 55 million people—a number projected to rise to 152 million by 2050. Current medications target Alzheimer's disease, the most prevalent form of dementia. This study investigated Juniperus phoenicea L., a plant used in traditional Chinese medicine, as a potential inhibitor of palmitoyl-protein thioesterase 1 (PPT1), an enzyme associated with dementia.MethodsJ.

pmc-12645908.title: Endosymbiosis in trypanosomatids: the bacterium regulates the intermediate and oxidative metabolism of the host cell
pmc-12645908.creator: Azuil Barrinha, Ana Carolina Loyola-Machado, Marlon Dias Mariano dos Santos, Paulo Costa Carvalho, Wanderley de Souza, Ana Paula Valente, Antonio Galina, Maria Cristina Machado Motta
pmc-12645908.description: Endosymbiosis in trypanosomatids involves a mutualistic association between a symbiotic bacterium and a host protozoan and represents an excellent model for studying metabolic coevolution and the origin of organelles. This work investigated the influence of the symbiont on the metabolism of Angomonas deanei by comparing wild-type and aposymbiotic strains under different nutritional conditions.

pmc-12729093.title: Newborn screening and referral for congenital anomalies by lay health workers in Pakistan: a mixed-methods study to evaluate the effectiveness of a co-created educational intervention
pmc-12729093.creator: Shazia Junejo, Mahwish Fatima, Ammar Ali Muhammad, Maryam Sherwani, Saima Ali, Tabassum Zehra, Lubna Samad
pmc-12729093.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundGlobally, 8 million babies are born with a congenital anomaly annually causing 240,000 neonatal deaths, with 95% disease burden in Low- and Middle-Income Countries (LMICs). Early neonatal screening, timely referral and management can lead to reduced disability and mortality. The WHO recommends employing lay health workers (HWs) as agents to promote health due to critical shortage of health service providers worldwide.

pmc-13073160.title: Perioperative Outcomes of Robotic Versus Conventional Total Laparoscopic Hysterectomy in Surgically Complex Cases: A Propensity Score-Matched Study
pmc-13073160.creator: Kyung Jin Eoh, Hyewon Hur, Joo Hyun Park
pmc-13073160.description: Objective: To compare perioperative outcomes between robotic and conventional total laparoscopic hysterectomy in terms of operative time, intraoperative blood loss, and postoperative recovery in surgically complex cases. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included patients that underwent total laparoscopic hysterectomy between 2020 and 2022.

pmc-13144226.title: JAK/STAT inhibition reprograms T cell activation and metabolism in inflammatory arthritis patients
pmc-13144226.creator: Viviana Marzaioli, Aenea A. I. Brugman, Niamh O’Dowd, Achilleas Floudas, Aine Gorman, Carl Orr, Douglas J. Veale, Ursula Fearon
pmc-13144226.description: ObjectivesInflammatory arthritis (IA) is a group of autoimmune diseases characterised by joint inflammation and progressive damage, thus impairing the patient’s quality of life. The JAK/STAT pathway inhibitor Tofacitinib has been successfully introduced into the clinic to treat patients with IA, however its direct effect on T cell responses is widely unknown.

pmc-13197279.title: Minimal chemical modification enables alpha/beta radiolabeling of sacituzumab govitecan for targeted therapy in high grade serous ovarian cancer
pmc-13197279.creator: Angelique Loor, Kyeara N. Mack, David Bauer, Aidan Ingham, Edwin C. Pratt, Jason S. Lewis
pmc-13197279.description: PurposeOvarian cancer (OC) is frequently diagnosed at late stages after metastasis and chemorefractive leading to poor survival outcomes. There is a critical need for earlier detection and novel antigen-targeted therapies to improve patient survival at all stages. TROP-2 is a transmembrane glycoprotein overexpressed in many cancers and presents a promising target for OC.

pmc-13278448.title: Quantitative evaluation of anti-sliding performance and dosage regulation of steel slag asphalt mixture facing service environment
pmc-13278448.creator: Zhiqiao Cheng, Ping Li, Jingsheng Pan

pmc-13394672.title: NRF2/xCT‐Mediated Antioxidant Adaptation Attenuates Apoptosis Induced by ASCT2 Inhibition in Prostate Cancer
pmc-13394672.creator: Jiaxing Wei, Yasutaka Yamada, Takaaki Tamura, Masahiro Sugiura, Xue Zhao, Meng Ni, Adilan Aierken, Tomokazu Sazuka, Yusuke Imamura, Shinichi Sakamoto
pmc-13394672.description: Glutamine supports biosynthesis and redox homeostasis in cancer cells. The glutamine transporter ASCT2 is highly expressed in prostate cancer and is associated with higher Gleason grade. Although ASCT2 inhibition induces reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and apoptosis, cancer cells may activate antioxidant adaptive mechanisms that limit therapeutic efficacy.

pmc-13491968.title: MutAIverse: an AI-powered, mechanism-backed platform for discovering novel DNA adducts and their precursor genotoxins
pmc-13491968.creator: Shiva Satija, Sanjay Kumar Mohanty, Sachin B Jorvekar, Anshul Verma, Saveena Solanki, Vishakha Gautam, Sakshi Arora, Aayushi Mittal, Arushi Sharma, Sonam Chauhan, Subhadeep Duari, Suvendu Kumar, Avdhesh Rai, Anupam Das, Kaberi Kakati, Kishore Das, Anupam Sarma, Juhi Tayal, Debarka Sengupta, Anurag Mehta, Roshan M Borkar, Gaurav Ahuja

pmc-13589197.title: Moxifloxacin‐Induced Bullous Acute Generalized Exanthematous Pustulosis (AGEP): A Case Report of a Rare Clinical Presentation
pmc-13589197.creator: Mehmet Yeral, Dilek Dasgin, Ceyda Tetik Aydogdu, Ekin Altinbas, Serkan Yasar Celik, Baris Bat
pmc-13589197.description: Acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis (AGEP) is a severe cutaneous adverse reaction (SCAR) typically characterized by sterile pustules. The bullous variant of AGEP is exceptionally rare and represents a significant diagnostic challenge as it clinically mimics toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN). We report the case of a 91‐year‐old woman who developed AGEP following moxifloxacin therapy, which rapidly progressed into a bullous form.

pmc-13633221.title: Is Digital Healthcare Better Than None? The Digital Health Technology Dilemma in Low-Income Countries
pmc-13633221.creator: Brandon Ferlito, Heidi Mertes
pmc-13633221.description: Digital health technologies (DHTs) are often promoted as solutions to healthcare access challenges in low-income countries (LICs), where a lack of infrastructure, healthcare professionals, and regulatory capacity makes them especially appealing. In such contexts, DHTs can provide services that would otherwise remain out of reach. Yet their implementation raises significant ethical and regulatory concerns.
